newsitem.title: USA: DuPont suspends Georgia mine plan.
newsitem.headline: DuPont suspends Georgia mine plan.

text.p: DuPont Co. said Friday it will suspend plans for a proposed titanium surface mining operation near the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge in southeast Georgia and consult with concerned environmental groups, government bodies and local citizens.

"We've heard the concerns that have been expressed and will intensify our interaction with interested stakeholders," said Ellen Kullman, vice president and general manager, DuPont White Pigment and Mineral Products.

"We will continue only if we can satisfy them -- and ourselves -- that we will do no harm to the Okefenokee. We agree that this unique ecosystem should be enjoyed and appreciated by generations to come," Kullman said.
The company said it plans to ask an independent third party to aid in its decision-making process.
DuPont owns or leases some 38,000 acres near Folkston, Ga., along a feature known as the Trail Ridge.
It said the ridge contains significant concentrations of high quality titanium minerals -- the key ingredient in titanium dioxide, a white pigment used primarily in paint, plastics and paper.
The company has conducted surface mining operations on the Trail Ridge in northeast Florida which are identical to what is proposed for Georgia.

"While we believe our mining operation can be conducted in a safe and environmentally sound manner, we recognise that we can proceed only if we have the support of those who are concerned about any potential impact on the refuge," Kullman said.
She added, "we're committed to stepping up the dialogue we began in 1994 so that all parties, including DuPont, can ultimately make an informed decision based on facts, not assumptions."
Kullman said the company would be open to "open to all possible outcomes, including the full range from mining to no mining, and we hope other participants will be as well."
